# `Q-1-1` — YAML Syntax Error

> The YAML document being parsed has a syntax error that prevents
> parsing.

## What this means

Quarto could not parse a YAML document — typically `_quarto.yml`,
the YAML front-matter at the top of a `.qmd` file, or a YAML block
inside a `.qmd` file. The text in that YAML region is not valid
YAML, so Quarto stops before reading any of its contents.

This is a *parser-level* error, raised before schema validation
runs. Errors like missing required properties (`Q-1-10`) or unknown
properties (`Q-1-18`) cannot be reported when the parser cannot
even get a document out of the text.

## Why this happens

The most common causes:

- **Mismatched indentation.** YAML uses indentation to indicate
  nesting. Mixing tabs and spaces, or jumping back to an outer
  level mid-block, makes the structure ambiguous.
- **Unquoted strings that contain reserved characters.** Values
  with `:`, `#`, `[`, `]`, `{`, `}`, or leading `*`, `&`, `!`
  typically need quotes.
- **Unclosed quotes or brackets.** A stray `"` or `[` with no
  matching close.
- **A flow-style sequence or mapping that is not well-formed**,
  e.g. `[a, b,, c]` or `{key: value,}`.

## How to fix

Read the error message: it includes the line and column where the
underlying YAML parser gave up. The cause is usually within a few
lines of that point — most often on the line itself, sometimes on
the preceding line.

If indentation is the suspect, replace tabs with spaces and align
keys at the same nesting level. YAML accepts any number of leading
spaces, but the *same* number for every key at the same level.

If a value contains punctuation that YAML reserves, wrap the value
in double quotes:

```yaml
title: "A: a study in punctuation"   # quoted because of the colon
```
